mark_breakdown.desc: Calculate side AD using tangent in triangle ACD
Calculate angle theta in triangle ADE using tangent
Calculate length AE and angle EAB
Calculate x using cosine in triangle ABE

subparts.solution: In triangle $ACD$, $\tan 40^\circ = \frac{AD}{8} \implies AD = 8\tan 40^\circ$. In triangle $ADE$, $\tan\theta = \frac{5}{AD} = \frac{5}{8\tan 40^\circ} \implies \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{8\tan 40^\circ}\right) \approx 36.68^\circ \approx 36.7^\circ$. Also, $\sin 36.68^\circ \approx \frac{5}{AE} \implies AE \approx \frac{5}{\sin 36.68^\circ}$. Now $D\hat{A}C = 90^\circ - 40^\circ = 50^\circ$ {angles in triangle $ACD$}, so $E\hat{A}B \approx 50^\circ + 36.68^\circ \approx 86.68^\circ$. In triangle $ABE$, $\cos E\hat{A}B = \frac{x}{AE} \implies \cos 86.68^\circ \approx \frac{x}{\frac{5}{\sin 36.68^\circ}} \implies x \approx \frac{5\cos 86.68^\circ}{\sin 36.68^\circ} \approx 0.485$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Apply trigonometric ratios sequentially across adjacent right-angled triangles sharing common sides.
step_by_step: Find angle $\theta$ and hypotenuse $AE$ in $\triangle ADE$.
Compute angle $D\hat{A}C$ and sum it with $\theta$ to determine angle $E\hat{A}B$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing which side is adjacent and opposite for angles measured at vertex $A$ versus other vertices.
